full_name: Nonconvex Variance-Reduced Conditional Gradient for Stochastic Optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Algorithm 7.13, Theorem 7.17, and Corollary 7.12)
formalization_notes: Corrected 2026-06-10: the previous JSON incorrectly promoted Corollary 7.12's constant stepsize and sqrt-batch specialization into the Algorithm 7.13/Theorem 7.17 object layer.
The repaired source model keeps Algorithm 7.13 and Theorem 7.17 general in the stepsize sequence {alpha_k} and batch-size condition b >= T.
Eq. (7.4.15) and b = T = sqrt(m) are recorded only as the Corollary 7.12 specialization, not as primitive data for Theorem 7.17.

problem.description: Nonconvex stochastic optimization over a compact convex set

assumptions.name: Almost sure L-smoothness
assumptions.math: F(\cdot, \xi) \text{ is a smooth function with Lipschitz constant } L \text{ for any } \xi \in \Xi \text{ almost surely}

assumptions.name: Paired gradient access
assumptions.math: \text{It is possible to generate a realization } \xi \in \Xi, \text{ and to compute } \nabla F(x, \xi) \text{ and } \nabla F(y, \xi) \text{ for any given two points } x, y \in X \text{ for a fixed realization } \xi

initialization.math: x_1 \in X, \; T, \; \{\alpha_k\}, \; \text{refresh sample size } m, \; \text{recursive mini-batch size } b

steps.name: Epoch refresh (if k % T == 1)
steps.math: \text{Generate i.i.d. sample } H^s = \{\xi_1^s, \ldots, \xi_m^s\}, \quad G_k = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} \nabla F(x_k, \xi_i^s), \quad s \leftarrow s + 1

steps.name: Recursive gradient update (otherwise)
steps.math: \text{Generate i.i.d. sample } I^k = \{\xi_1^k, \ldots, \xi_b^k\}, \quad G_k = \frac{1}{b} \sum_{i=1}^{b} \left( \nabla F(x_k, \xi_i^k) - \nabla F(x_{k-1}, \xi_i^k) \right) + G_{k-1}

parameters.name: \{\alpha_k\}
parameters.math: \{\alpha_k\}_{k=1}^{N} \text{ is the general stepsize sequence used by Algorithm 7.13 and Theorem 7.17}

main_theorem.rate: Theorem 7.17 is the general convergence bound. Complexity rates are obtained only after the Corollary 7.12 specialization.

proof.description: Use smoothness of f with the convex combination update x_{k+1} = (1 - alpha_k)x_k + alpha_k y_k to derive the one-step descent inequality
proof.math: f(x_{k+1}) \le f(x_k) + \alpha_k \langle G_k, y_k - x_k \rangle + \frac{1}{2L} \|\delta_k\|^2 + L \alpha_k^2 \|y_k - x_k\|^2

proof.description: Combine the descent inequality with the Wolfe-gap surrogate (7.4.2) to bound gap(x_k) by the linear oracle term plus estimator error
Apply the stochastic estimator variance bound (Lemma 7.5) to replace (6.5.16) in the Theorem 7.16 proof, obtaining the stochastic bound of Theorem 7.17

corollary_specializations.name: Corollary 7.12
corollary_specializations.proof_role: Specializes Theorem 7.17 by substituting Eq. (7.4.15), using \sum_{k=1}^{N}\alpha_k=N\alpha, \sum_{k=1}^{N}\alpha_k^2=N\alpha^2, and bounding the epoch maximum term by 2N\alpha^2.
corollary_specializations.formalization_warning: This specialization must not be used as the definition of Algorithm 7.13 or Theorem 7.17. It is a corollary-level parameter regime.

key_lemmas.name: Wolfe-gap upper bound
key_lemmas.role: Bounds the true Wolfe gap by the linear oracle model gap plus the estimator error times the diameter

proof.description: Start from the Wolfe-gap definition and write nabla f(x_k) = G_k - delta_k
proof.math: \operatorname{gap}(x_k) = \max_{x \in X} \langle \nabla f(x_k), x_k - x \rangle = \max_{x \in X} \langle G_k - \delta_k, x_k - x \rangle

proof.description: Bound the perturbation term using the feasible-set diameter

key_lemmas.name: Epochwise estimator variance bound (Lemma 7.5)
key_lemmas.role: Bounds the expected squared error of the recursive gradient estimator within each epoch for the stochastic setting

proof.description: Within one epoch, expand the recursive definition of G_k and isolate the centered mini-batch gradient-difference noise plus the batch-refresh noise from the epoch start
Use almost sure L-smoothness, independence of the fresh samples, and the variance bound (7.4.13) to control the recursive term by iterate differences and the refresh term by sigma^2/m

key_lemmas.name: Finite-sum nonconvex CG bound (Theorem 7.16)
key_lemmas.role: Provides the finite-sum nonconvex conditional gradient convergence bound that serves as the template for the stochastic extension

proof.description: Use smoothness of f with the update x_{k+1} = (1 - alpha_k)x_k + alpha_k y_k to derive the one-step inequality (7.4.5), then combine with the Wolfe-gap surrogate (7.4.2)
proof.math: f(x_{k+1}) \le f(x_k) + \alpha_k \langle G_k, y_k - x_k \rangle + \frac{1}{2L}\|\delta_k\|^2 + L\alpha_k^2 \bar{D}_X^2

proof.description: Substitute the finite-sum estimator variance bound (Lemma 7.4), sum over iterations inside an epoch, control the double sums, and telescope over epochs
